title: Data Streaming with Kafka&Flink
short: Predicting 3D protein structure from sequence using message-passing networks.
body:
### Introduction Data is being generated every day at an unprecedented scale. Batch and streaming data are two of the most prevalent forms of data, each originating from different sources and generation processes. In recent years, the ability to capture and process streaming data has become increasingly important, as it enables organizations to gain real-time insights and supports analysts in making faster, more informed decisions.

Motivation

### Motivation Building an effective real-time stream processing pipeline requires the ability to combine different technologies into a reliable and well-designed technology stack. This project was motivated by the desire to gain a deeper understanding of the available tools and to apply them in practice by building a complete real-time data processing workflow. Such systems can provide insights with sub-second latency, enabling faster and more informed decision-making. Real-time stream processing is particularly valuable in use cases such as fraud detection, Internet of Things (IoT) applications, real-time monitoring, and other scenarios where immediate access to data is essential.

Method

### Method This project uses a combination of open-source technologies, including Apache Kafka, Apache Flink, Apache Superset, and Debezium for Change Data Capture (CDC). The data originates from a MySQL source database. Debezium captures changes in the database and publishes them as events to a Kafka topic. Apache Flink then continuously consumes these events, processes the incoming data, and writes the results to a target database. Finally, Apache Superset is used to visualize and analyze the processed data in real time. This architecture enables changes in the source database to flow through the entire pipeline with minimal latency, from data capture and stream processing to real-time analysis and visualization.

Results

### Results The infrastructure developed in this project enables real-time monitoring and detection of potentially fraudulent activities. The implemented streaming pipeline can identify suspicious transactions and generate real-time alerts and logs, allowing potential fraud to be detected and investigated with minimal delay. This demonstrates how a real-time data processing stack can support fraud detection and improve the ability to respond quickly to suspicious activities. .
